pgpz-november-9.markdown:
Hi everyone, here's last week's update.

Originally posted at [Weekly Policy Memo: November 9, 2026 | PGPZ Community](https://pgpz.org/updates/2026-11-09-weekly-policy-memo). 

Last week's policy memo covers SEC and CFTC Commissioner nominees; DOJ and industry groups challenging IL's digital asset tax; and Rep. Tom Emmer's election as Minority Whip of 120th Congress. 

**Key Takeaways**

* Senate Agriculture will hear CFTC nominees Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland on November 17. Senate Banking will hear SEC nominees Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine on November 19.
* DOJ and industry groups backed the Illinois digital asset tax challenge. Enforcement is stayed until July 1, 2027, under the existing order.
* House Republicans elected Tom Emmer, a champion for digital assets in Congress, was elected as Minority Whip for the next Congress.

**Action Items**

* No action items at this time.

**[X Post of the Week](https://x.com/Grayscale/status/2120235280720621854):**

**[![image|237x315](upload://i7VftaRvtgGVAjI4lX67BuGCnQe.jpeg)](https://x.com/Grayscale/status/2120235280720621854)**

**[Senate Committees Schedule SEC and CFTC Nomination Hearings](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/13/u-s-senate-banking-committee-races-toward-hearing-on-new-sec-nominations)**

The Senate Agriculture Committee will hear Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) nominees Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland on November 17 at 3:00 pm ET, and the Senate Banking Committee will hear Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) nominees Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine at its November 19 session, which begins at 10:00 am ET. President Donald Trump submitted all four nominations on November 12.

**Why it matters for Zcash:**

New commissioners at both of these agencies would help decide how the agencies apply existing law to digital assets and would improve regulations’ durability as each agency’s nominees include a Republican and a Democrat.

Johnson is a former CFTC commissioner and Levine previously served as deputy chief of staff to SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Both CFTC nominees previously worked on the CLARITY Act in their respective Senate Agriculture Committee roles.

**Action Item:**

No action item at this time.

**Relevant Post:**

**[![image|236x230](upload://8QVjrdk4tr8nikC99fnNFNZf8dD.jpeg)](http://x.com/ElleBeyoud/status/2121005472719180202)**

 

**[Justice Department and Industry Back Illinois Digital Asset Tax Challenge](https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-justice-department-business-groups-defi-illinois-crypto-tax)**

The U.S. Department of Justice filed a statement of interest on November 6 urging an Illinois circuit court to reject the state’s Digital Asset Tax Act. It argued that the Act singles out digital assets and imposes burdensome liability. The U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA) submitted an amicus brief challenging the tax under the Internet Tax Freedom Act and the Commerce Clause. On November 11, a coalition led by the DeFi Education Fund asked to file a separate brief. It argued that Illinois’ draft rules could reach software providers that cannot identify users or collect the tax.

The Act taxes covered brokerage services involving exchange, transfer or storage at 0.2% of the asset’s value. A gain or change in beneficial ownership is not necessary. The court’s agreed order stays the tax’s effect and enforcement until July 1, 2027, six months after the statutory start date. The filings give the court additional legal and technical arguments; they do not decide whether the tax will ultimately take effect.

**Why it matters for Zcash:**

If the tax takes effect as written, a covered broker’s transfer of ZEC to a customer’s own wallet could trigger a charge even though the customer still owns the same assets. The case also raises a separate question for wallet developers and network operators. A provider that does not handle customer assets may have no way to know where a user lives or withhold tax from a transfer. Imposing those duties could push providers to collect identity or location data they do not otherwise need. That concern applies to the design of self-custody tools as well as access to shielded payments through regulated services.

**Action Item:**

No action item at this time.

**Relevant Post:**

**[![image|235x320](upload://b1hpJrBqXCr2l1jBZLb1ilIKsKf.jpeg)](https://x.com/_jikim/status/2120952727752921213?a=8yAJdp1JqVL-OP4mZMM&s=20)**

 

**[Tom Emmer Elected House Republican Minority Whip](https://cointelegraph.com/news/crypto-ally-tom-emmer-elected-house-gop-minority-whip)**

House Republicans elected Rep. Tom Emmer (R-MN) Minority Whip on November 10 for the 120th Congress, which begins January 3. Rep. Emmer is the current Majority Whip and will continue to organize Republican votes under incoming Minority Leader Jim Jordan. Rep. Emmer is an original House co-sponsor of the CLARITY Act and the initial sponsor of the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA).

**Why it matters for Zcash:**

Rep. Emmer’s position gives him a role in coordinating Republican support for legislation and amendments. With Democrats taking the House majority, committee chairs and majority leadership will determine what moves forward. Rep. Emmer has a history of working across party lines to obtain bipartisan support for legislation and has been a steadfast supporter of the digital asset industry.

**Action Item:**

No action item at this time.

pgpz-november-2.author: Divij Pandya
pgpz-november-2.markdown:
Hi everyone, here's this week's update.

Originally posted at [Weekly Policy Memo: November 2, 2026 | PGPZ Community](https://pgpz.org/updates/2026-11-02-weekly-policy-memo).

This week's policy memo covers the U.S. midterm elections; SEC staff providing clarity on ecosystem centralization; HFSC Dems working on a new market structure proposal; an upcoming SEC proposed rule on broker-dealers and recordkeeping undergoing review ahead of public release; and FinCEN and the Federal Reserve withdrawing their 2020 rule that proposed lowering amount threshold required for certain data collection.

**Key Takeaways**

* Democrats have won control of the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate, according to election reporting, setting up a divided government when the 120th Congress begins on January 3, 2027.
* SEC staff added three crypto-asset FAQs on November 2. For the Commission’s “digital commodity” interpretation, unaffiliated participants in broad-based governance generally are not considered a controlling group merely because they vote, including through a foundation, absent a separate agreement to coordinate.
* House Financial Services Democratic staff are developing an unpublished market-structure proposal drawing on Rep. Maxine Waters’ 2025 Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights amendment and subsequent Senate negotiations.
* A key agency tasked with reviewing regulatory proposals received an SEC proposal regarding broker-dealer financial recordkeeping and reporting, among other things. It concerns how registered firms safeguard customer assets, maintain financial resources, and preserve records when handling crypto assets.
* FinCEN announced that it and the Federal Reserve are withdrawing their October 2020 proposal on funds-transfer recordkeeping and the Travel Rule. The proposal would have lowered the relevant threshold from $3,000 to $250 for transfers beginning or ending outside the United States, and expressly addressed convertible virtual currencies and digital assets with legal tender status.

**Action Item**

* Please reach out if you have questions about the midterm election results and the impact on the Zcash ecosystem.

**November 2026 Midterm Elections Update:**

Democrats have won control of the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate, according to election reporting, setting up a divided government when the 120th Congress begins on January 3, 2027. President Trump will remain in office.

The 120th Congress is an opportunity to educate new and incumbent lawmakers about Zcash, financial privacy, self-custody, and developer protections, but it will be an uphill battle given the growing backlash towards crypto, particularly “big crypto.” Prominent Democrats have already previewed that the next two years will be marked by investigations into the Trump administration, and that includes crypto companies affiliated with the administration and Trump family.

Read the full article on the Zcash Community Forum ( https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/november-2026-u-s-midterm-elections/58887 ) or on X ( https://x.com/pgpzcash/status/2118130438225211872 ).

**Why this matters for Zcash:**

For the Zcash ecosystem, the most consequential outcome is the forthcoming change in House and Senate committee leadership. Leadership decides which bills move forward and what those bills must contain. Our assessment is that broader crypto legislation, such as market structure legislation, will face tougher negotiations, while scrutiny of financial privacy and illicit finance are likely to increase. Narrower agreements on developer protections and other issues remain possible, but this will be more difficult to achieve, particularly when compared against the CLARITY Act negotiations, which saw the removal of key Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA) provisions. The BRCA clarifies that noncustodial blockchain developers are not money transmitters under the Bank Secrecy Act, and an important part of the legislation that shielded blockchain developers from criminal liability was removed prior to the Senate’s September 15 procedural vote.

**Action Item:**

Please reach out if you have questions about the midterm election results and the impact on the Zcash ecosystem.

**[X Post of the Week](https://x.com/Zcash/status/2118534331090284580):**

**[![image|218x172](upload://nXVncCh47HDvkZP3357sEIkVimP.jpeg)](https://x.com/Zcash/status/2118534331090284580)**

**[SEC Staff Distinguishes Independent Governance From Centralized Control](https://www.sec.gov/about/divisions-offices/division-corporation-finance/faqs-crypto-assets)**

The SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance added three crypto-asset FAQs on November 2. For the Commission’s “digital commodity” interpretation, unaffiliated participants in broad-based governance generally are not considered a controlling group merely because they vote, including through a foundation, absent a separate agreement to coordinate. Delegation can still be relevant. Staff identifies unilateral authority over access, voting procedures, consensus participation or transaction reversal as evidence of oversight. It also distinguishes a system’s functionality from decentralization. The clarification offers a more specific framework for assessing control, but remains nonbinding staff guidance, creates no new obligations.

**Why it matters for Zcash:**

For the ecosystem, the practical inquiry is who can exercise authority over a network or application. Community voting, grant administration, and the existence of a foundation should be assessed through their actual powers and relationships. Moreover, a token-voting label alone cannot establish independence. This is relevant to evaluating governance proposals; it is not an SEC classification of ZEC or approval of a particular arrangement.

**Action Item:**

No action item at this time.

**Relevant Post:**

**[![image|218x64](upload://1BnCv5mYTEPIDxLZerTMNbuK8n9.jpeg)](https://x.com/propelforward/status/2117321446137733271)**

**[Election Results Change the Congressional Market-Structure Debate](https://www.cryptoinamerica.com/p/house-democrats-eye-new-crypto-market)**

Crypto In America reports that House Financial Services Democratic staff are developing an unpublished market-structure proposal drawing on Rep. Maxine Waters’ 2025 Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights amendment and subsequent Senate negotiations. Discussions reportedly envisage a larger SEC role and a more limited CFTC role than the CLARITY Act, alongside consumer protection and ethics provisions. Treatment of decentralized finance remains disputed. Note that a Democratic majority would strengthen agenda-setting power, but enactment would still require negotiations with Republicans and the administration.

**Why it matters for Zcash:**

This is an opportunity to discuss how Zcash can promote effective consumer protection (e.g., via data minimization), lawful financial privacy, and clear distinctions between custodial intermediaries and people who publish or maintain noncustodial software.

**Action Item:**

No action item at this time.

**Relevant Post:**

[![image|218x203](upload://mRLZZVT2b5iQzLSWT0PPJr8fQad.jpeg)](https://x.com/EleanorTerrett/status/2118041922011021418)

**[SEC Crypto Broker-Dealer Proposal Enters White House Review](https://thedefiant.io/converge/regulation/sec-crypto-broker-rule-enters-white-house-review)**

A key agency tasked with reviewing regulatory proposals before they are published received the SEC’s proposed “Amendments to Broker-Dealer Financial Responsibility and Recordkeeping and Reporting Rules Regarding Crypto Assets.” White House review is an important procedural step toward a possible public proposal. The regulatory agenda identifies potential amendments to net-capital and customer-protection rules, together with broker-dealer recordkeeping rules. These subjects concern how registered firms safeguard customer assets, maintain financial resources and preserve records when handling crypto assets.

**Why it matters for Zcash:**

For registered intermediaries considering ZEC-related services, clearer capital, custody, and recordkeeping treatment could affect the feasibility and cost of offering those services. The effects will depend on the proposal’s scope and the legal treatment of the assets and activities involved. Additionally, the recordkeeping component warrants attention to data security and financial privacy.

**Action Item:**

No action item at this time.

**Relevant Post:**

**[![image|218x195](upload://jPcMwWthhZPTwmgJmYcjAfVA4Zp.jpeg)](https://x.com/laurashin/status/2118667225913868335)**

**[FinCEN and Federal Reserve Withdraw the 2020 Travel Rule Proposal](https://www.fincen.gov/news/news-releases/fincen-announces-withdrawal-proposed-rule-related-recordkeeping-and-travel-rule)**

FinCEN announced that it and the Federal Reserve are withdrawing their October 2020 proposal on funds-transfer recordkeeping and the Travel Rule. The proposal would have lowered the relevant threshold from $3,000 to $250 for transfers beginning or ending outside the United States, and expressly addressed convertible virtual currencies and digital assets with legal tender status. The withdrawal notice is scheduled for Federal Register publication on November 9, when it becomes effective.

The agencies cite the age of the proposal, changes in digital asset markets and emerging legal frameworks, and the value of fresh public input before adopting similar amendments. They will not finalize this NPRM, and any renewed proposal would require another opportunity for comment. The notice records concerns about compliance costs, remittances and retention of personally identifiable information. Existing recordkeeping and Travel Rule obligations remain in place. The action removes a pending expansion of information collection rather than creating a general exemption for crypto transactions.

**Why it matters for Zcash:**

Avoiding a lower threshold limits an additional source of identity data collection and transmission by covered institutions. That is relevant to Zcash users who interact with regulated services, because unnecessary copies of sensitive information can increase exposure to breaches and misuse.

**Action Item:**

No action item at this time.

**Relevant Post:**

**[![image|218x254](upload://tE5k7Ttm2rRnvOXPO94ZPysvima.jpeg)](https://x.com/ADLXBT/status/2118730969834541179)**

pgpz-international-advocates.author: Divij Pandya
pgpz-international-advocates.markdown:
All, as discussed in our October report [post](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/grant-application-pretty-good-policy-for-zcash/57134/17), PGPZ is working on a global policy report that will set out public policy principles supporting Zcash and financial privacy, examine the regulatory landscape across participating jurisdictions, and recommend changes to help each jurisdiction align with those principles.

So far, the work covers the United States and Brazil (and Mexico hopefully soon). We’d like to expand that coverage and connect with people interested in strengthening Zcash-focused advocacy internationally.

Please reach out if you have relevant policy experience or local knowledge or work with government affairs professionals, attorneys, or other advocates who might be interested. We welcome both contributors and introductions to potential collaborators.

Contributions could include helping draft or review a jurisdiction’s section, explaining how local laws affect the Zcash ecosystem, identifying opportunities for policy reform, or connecting us with local government affairs/policy experts.

We’re tentatively targeting January 2027 for publication. If you’d like to contribute or know someone we should speak with, please reply here, send me a direct message, or email me at div@pgpz.org.

pgpz-october-report.author: Divij Pandya
pgpz-october-report.markdown:
All, here's our October monthly report. 

Much of the admin work is complete, while meetings, educational events, and public engagement remain ongoing.

Here’s where we stand against each commitment:

 1. **Establish the Board of Directors — completed in September.** We established PGPZ’s Board and worked through how its governance and leadership can best support our mission.

 2. **Complete necessary lobbying, legal, tax, accounting, insurance, and compliance reviews — completed in October.** These reviews helped put the organizational foundation in place for our advocacy work.

 3. **Establish separate project accounting and operations processes through the Financial Privacy Foundation (FPF) — completed in September.** We’re grateful to FPF for its support in getting PGPZ up and running.

 4. **Publish an initial policy agenda and policy-position process — prepared; publication pending.** We drafted these in September and finalized them in October. I’ll be sharing them with our Board this month before posting the non-confidential information here on the Forum.

 5. **Create foundational educational materials — completed in September and expanded in October.** We’ve developed materials to introduce Zcash, explain practical uses of financial privacy, and describe the policy issues affecting the ecosystem.

 6. **Develop a stakeholder and policymaker-engagement database — completed in October.** This supports our outreach, prioritization, and follow-up with congressional offices, agencies, and other stakeholders.

 7. **Conduct at least 15 introductory meetings — in progress.** Our first congressional fly-in took place around the Cypherpunk Policy Dinner and DC Privacy Summit. Paul, in his role as PGPZ’s Chairman, and I met with four key offices: Republican Senate Banking Committee staff, a Democratic Senate office focused on developer protections, and two senior Republican offices whose Members serve on the House Financial Services Committee and focus on financial privacy.
    Candidly, this was smaller than I had hoped. These were valuable introductory conversations, but we still have work to do to reach the meeting target and build sustained relationships. Further outreach is underway with 20ish meetings planned in mid-November.

 8. **Host at least one educational briefing or workshop — planned for November.**

 9. **Continue publishing weekly public policy updates — ongoing.** We’re continuing to publish updates on developments relevant to Zcash, financial privacy, and developer protections.

10. **Establish a process for ecosystem participants to submit policy concerns and technical input — established in September and October, with ongoing engagement.** I’ve been posting comment-letter outlines and other materials on the Forum to invite input. Email is generally the best way to reach me because it lands directly in my inbox, but I also monitor the Forum and X for comments and feedback. Please keep sharing concerns, providing technical context, and asking policy questions.

Beyond these commitments, October provided several opportunities to build relationships and expand our work.

The Cypherpunk Policy Dinner was a huge success, and we were fortunate to have former SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce join us. Thank you to everyone who participated and helped make it happen. At the DC Privacy Summit, we also had productive conversations with attendees from other organizations about potential collaboration to advance financial privacy.

Zcon was another valuable opportunity to build on this work and connect with advocates across the ecosystem.

One project coming out of these conversations is a global policy report. The report will set out policy principles supporting Zcash and financial privacy, examine the regulatory landscape across participating jurisdictions, and recommend changes that would help each jurisdiction align with those principles. So far, the work covers the United States and Brazil.

At Zcon, I was fortunate to meet Palmar from Zcash Mexico, who suggested an advocate I can connect with about contributing to the report and collaborating on other advocacy efforts. I’ll shortly post a separate Forum invitation seeking contributors from additional jurisdictions, with the goal of expanding Zcash-focused advocacy internationally.

We’re tentatively targeting January 2027 for publication. If you have relevant policy experience or local knowledge (or know someone who does) and would like to contribute, please let me know. 

As always, please let me know if you have any questions.

Best,

Div

pgpz-policy-questions.author: Divij Pandya
pgpz-policy-questions.markdown:
Hi all,

One of Pretty Good Policy for Zcash’s (PGPZ) objectives is to keep ecosystem stakeholders informed about public policy and regulatory developments in Washington, DC (and globally soon). I haven’t seen a dedicated thread for these topics, so I’m starting one to facilitate discussion. We can also schedule live sessions/weekly office hours if there's interest. Accordingly, please:

* Post questions here for public-policy/regulatory updates and discussion.
* Re: office hours/live Q&A, let me know whether Fridays at 1pm EST (or another date/time) work?
* For urgent matters, DM/email me directly at div@pgpz.org; otherwise, the thread is the best place for ongoing questions and coordination.

I’d also like to use this channel to coordinate on comment letter responses and other feedback that can support public policy development. 

As a reminder, we post our weekly policy memos here (usually Fridays): https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/pgpz-community-weekly-policy-memos/56324 

And our grant details are available here: https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/grant-application-pretty-good-policy-for-zcash/57134 .

Please let me know if you have any questions or feedback. We're a dedicated resource for the ecosystem and for any advocacy needs you have.

Best,

Div
